RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday,  the March 13, 2008/Phalguna 23, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; Development of North Eastern Region;
Environment and Forests; External Affairs; Housing and
Urban Poverty Alleviation; Overseas Indian Affairs;
Panchayati Raj; Personnel, Public Grievances and
Pensions; Planning; Shipping, Road Transport
and Highways; Space; Statistics and
Programme Implementation;
Urban Development; Youth
Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
62
Support to schemes for the poor
*201. SHRI R. SHUNMUGA-
SUNDARAM: Will the Minister of
HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the schemes under which the State
Governments are being supported while
providing alternative houses for the slum
dwellers; and
(b) whether there are schemes executed
by his Ministry where the dilapidated
houses of the poor are either repaired or
rebuilt?
Status of Commonwealth Games,
2010
*202. DR. VIJAY MALLYA: Will the
Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND
SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) the status in respect of preparation
of the 2010 Commonwealth Games to be
held in our country;
(b) the additional infrastructure that
would be added for the games; and
(c) the support given by Government
to Indian teams in various disciplines in
respect of preparation for the 2010 games?
Sports infrastructure in Orissa
*203. SHRI BHAGIRATHI MAJHI:
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS
AND SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has extended
any financial assistance to Orissa for sports
infrastructure development during the last
four years;
(b) if so, the details of projects/
proposals for which Government has
extended the grant/financial assistance to
Orissa during the last four years;
(c) whether any such projects/
proposals are pending with Government
for consideration from Orissa at present;

63
(d) if so, by when all these pending
proposals/projects would be considered;
(e) whether Government has any
technical hurdle to consider these pending
projects; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Inclusion of Warangal and Tirupati
under JNNURM
*204. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Andhra Pradesh has requested the Union
Government to include two cities of
Warangal and Tirupati in 'C' category of
select cities under Jawaharlal Nehru
National Urban Renewal Mission
(JNNURM);
(b) if so, the complete details in this
regard;
(c) the response of the Union
Government in this regard; and
(d) by when this request is likely to be
given clearance?
Spectrum controversy
*205. SHRIMA TI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the country's National
Security Advisor was asked to step in to
resolve spectrum controversy and has met
Department of Telecommunications,
Telecom Regulatory Authority and Telecom
in the month of February to discuss the
issue;
(b) if so, the outcome of the discussions
held;
(c) whether all the hurdles that were
preventing clearance of spectrum have been
removed; and
(d) if so, by when final decision about
the spectrum is considered?
Eleventh Plan outlay
*206. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether National Development
Council has, recently, approved the
Eleventh Plan outlays for various sectors;
(b) if so, the details thereof alongwith
the details of the outlays;
(c) the reasons for late convening of
NDC even when the Eleventh Plan started
in April, 2007 and, as a result, the
allocations for various sectors would
actually start in 2009 only; and
(d) the action proposed to be taken
against those responsible for the late
convening of NDC?
Central assistance for drinking water
in cities
*207. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a proposal under
consideration of Government to provide
assistance to ten cities in the country which
would undertake to provide drinking water
to the population throughout the day and
all the seven days in the week, i.e. on 24x7
basis;
(b) if so, the names of cities where such
projects are proposed to be undertaken and
the basis on which Central assistance is to
be provided; and
(c) by when the projects are likely to be
completed?

64
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Green India Campaign
†*208. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI:
DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Green
India Campaign is being run by Government
for implementing strategy to meet the
climate change;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
environment of forests has become
unbalanced by uncontrolled afforestation
of Precipus Juli flora (Foreign Babool) in
Rajasthan, whose effect is reflecting as
constant decline in wildlife and medicinal
plants in the forests; and
(d) whether there is any scheme to take
help of voluntary agencies alongwith the
forest officers working in States on
afforestation under Green India Campaign?
Policy for allocation of spectrum
*209. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
SHRI HARISH RAWA T:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has evolved a
transparent and equitable policy for
allocation of spectrum, as announced by
the Prime Minister at the inauguration of
the 'India Telecom — 2007', on December
12, 2007;
(b) the details thereof indicating the
precise nature and substance of the
controversy; and
(c) the steps taken in the light of such a
policy?
Supply of uranium from Australia
†*210. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Australia has given
indications to India to stop the supply of
uranium;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the reaction of Government thereto?
Pressure on drainage system in Delhi
†*211. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARW AL: W ill the Minister of
URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government is aware of
heavy pressure on drainage system in Delhi
and other States;
(b) whether density of these drains
results in water-logging and floods in Delhi;
(c) if so, the names of areas which have
mainly been affected by this density of
drainage system during the last three years
till date in other States including the NCT
of Delhi;
(d) the main reasons for density of
drainage; and
(e) the steps taken to solve the problem
arising out of the density of the drainage
system?
Second and third generation of
spectrum
*212. SHRI S. S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:

65
(a) whether Government has decided to
allocate the second and third generation of
spectrum for mobile phone services;
(b) if so, the salient details of the criteria
for the allocation;
(c) whether TRAI accorded concurrence
to the said decision;
(d) if so, the salient details of its
concurrence;
(e) if not, the details of its objections
and suggestions;
(f) the steps taken, if any, in response
to TRAI's objections/suggestions;
(g) whether Department of
Telecommunications (DoT) had to entrust
the Telecom Engineering Centre (TEC) to
fix criteria for spectrum allotment;
(h) if so, the background details thereof;
and
(i) the criteria fixed by TEC?
Vadodara-Mumbai Expressway
*213. SHRI KESHUBHAI S. PA TEL:
SHRI SURENDRA MOTILAL
PATEL:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the progress made subsequent to the
declaration in Parliament for taking up the
work of Vadodara-Mumbai Expressway;
(b) the phases of planning and
implementation;
(c) whether it is a fact that the State
Government of Gujarat had frozen land of
300 m width along the proposed alignment
of V adodara-Mumbai Expressway as back
as in 1991; and
(d) if so, by when the acquisition of
land would be started?
Employees of PSUs
*214. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI MOHAMMED AMIN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of permanent employees
working in PSUs under the administrative
control of his Ministry as on the 31st
March, 2007, unit-wise breakup; and
(b) the number of contract/casual/
contingency workers working in these units
as on the 31st March, 2007?
Steps to stop illegal migration
*215. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether attention of Government
has been drawn to the illegal migration to
various countries where the migrants are
surviving in conditions unfit for human
habitation, working at extremely low
wages, suffering torture, exploitation,
depression and death; and
(b) the steps Government has taken in
this regard and stop the illegal trading and
arresting them?
Rising property prices
*216. DR. M. A. M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the real estate property
prices are rising rapidly in the country;
(b) if so, the rise in real estate property
prices during the last three years;

66
(c) the reasons for such rise in prices of
real estate properties;
(d) whether Government proposes to
set up any regulatory body to regulate the
real estate sector;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
Implementation of Y amuna Action
Plan
*217. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) the progres so far made in the
implementation of the Yamuna Action Plan
and the expenditure incurred thereon so far;
(b) whether the Plan has so far failed in
its object; and
(c) if so, the reasons therefor?
Overseas Employment Promotion
Council
*218. SHRI T. T. V . DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to set up
Overseas Employment Promotion Council
to regulate employment;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Preservation of Yamuna
*219. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI :
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether  Government is aware that
Government of NCT of Delhi has experts'
proposal how best to preserve the good
old Yamuna;
(b) if so, the salient features of the
proposal; and
(c) to what extent the proposal is
feasible to be made effective and at what
cost?
Nepalese stake on 'no-man's-land'
*220. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that during
December 2007 about 200 Maoist ultras
from Nepal staked their claim on a stretch
of 'no-man's-land' in Uttarakhand and
hoisted their red flag in a town in border
district of Champavat;
(b) if so, whether the border-pillars are
not existing in this area; and
(c) whether Government would conduct
a joint survey between Nepal and India to
demarcate the border so that such incidents
do not recur and border-pillars are duly
fixed to identify Indo-Nepalese border?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 7th March, 2008 Secretary-General.
Phalguna 17, 1929 (Saka)
